translations.answer: The original author defined the output as a=[base-frame linear acceleration, base-frame angular acceleration, joint accelerations], and the maintainer confirmed it is correct. Therefore, cannot directly take the first six dimensions of aba as world-frame base acceleration. The thread did not provide a local-to-world acceleration transformation, and did not clarify the difference between classical and spatial acceleration. When these quantities are involved, they must be verified against the target API definition.
translations.applicability: Applies to the original post Pinocchio floating-base aba() output explanation; cannot extrapolate to unmentioned classical acceleration interface.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for the environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author listed a=[local base linear acceleration, local base angular acceleration, joint accelerations], and the maintainer confirmed it.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Interpreted aba as a generalized acceleration in the generalized space of the base local frame, and verified the root joint local coordinate convention.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Interpreted the first six dimensions of aba as base local frame generalized acceleration; explicit world-frame transformation is required when world-frame quantities are needed.
translations.details.environments.0: 2022 Pinocchio floating-base dynamics; specific version and robot not mentioned.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread did not provide a local-to-world acceleration transformation, and did not discuss the difference between spatial acceleration, classical acceleration, and d(v)/dt.
translations.details.limits.1: Specific root joint type and software version not mentioned.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The maintainer confirmed the local coordinate interpretation of the first six dimensions of aba is correct.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: What coordinate system should the first six dimensions of aba() be interpreted in when returning floating base generalized acceleration?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Misinterpretation of generalized acceleration as a world-frame second-order position derivative.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The user is aware of the floating base linear velocity components in the local joint frame, but is uncertain whether the acceleration is expressed in the same way.
